clue.text: Exasperate trumpeters, etc, backstage?

parts.note: trumpeters, trombonists and the like make up the brass section of an orchestra
a performer who is backstage is off, out of sight of the audience

explanation.surface: A wry question whether musicians hidden behind the scenes are what annoys someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial verb meaning to irritate or thoroughly annoy someone.

clue.text: See feet in space under roof

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at how much floor area an attic offers.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room or storage area just beneath a house's roof.

clue.text: Double pound to replace centre of glittering old coin

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for glittering is swapped out for something else

parts.note: something glittering is shining

indicators.note: double means the letter for pound is written twice

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Sounds like a recipe for turning money into a gleaming antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: SHINING has seven letters; its central N gives way to LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-decimal British coin worth twelve pence, withdrawn after 1971.

clue.text: Gear seen around loch?

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake, and the gear in question is the traditional pleated Highland garment worn there

explanation.definitionFit: Highland dress, the tartan skirt-like garment typically seen in Scotland, home of lochs.

clue.text: Blatantly disregard wingers in football, not at home

indicators.note: wingers play on the edges of the pitch, so they are the outside letters of the word

parts.note: someone not at home is out

explanation.surface: A football report about wide players ignoring rules away from their home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To openly defy or show contempt for a rule or convention.

clue.text: Number one source of pain is back wearing away

indicators.note: back says the assembled letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a sore is a painful spot

explanation.surface: A sufferer's main complaint is a bad back that is gradually worsening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like a single phrase meaning chief, but it gives NO and I separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual destruction of rock or soil by wind, water or friction.

clue.text: Strangely silent, try to detect noise

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the next word are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: In an eerie quiet, someone strains to hear a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay attention with the ears in an effort to hear something.

clue.text: Fear mistake after first sign of trouble

indicators.note: after says the word for mistake follows the trouble letter
the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a mistake is an error

explanation.surface: Dread at having blundered as soon as problems appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme fright or dread; a synonym for great fear.

clue.text: One adopted by identical South East Asian cat?

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the one letter goes inside the word for identical

parts.note: identical means the same
the Roman numeral for one is I
SE is the compass abbreviation for South East

explanation.surface: A pet cat taken in by an Asian family from the South East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South East Asian' reads as one phrase, but South East gives SE and Asian cat is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of cat originating in Thailand, formerly called Siam; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Revise guesses, partly to make a transition

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice to rethink one's guesses so as to move smoothly to something new.
explanation.definitionFit: To move seamlessly from one topic, scene or piece of music into the next.

clue.text: Very soft substance of chapter after short story

indicators.note: after says the chapter letter follows the shortened story
short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A textbook line about which soft material a chapter covers after a brief tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum, the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale, rated one.

clue.text: Head off and hire a supporter

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of head are jumbled

parts.note: to hire something is to rent it

explanation.surface: A mutinous instruction to sack the boss and take on a loyal follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a phrasal verb meaning intercept, but 'off' is the anagram signal for HEAD, giving ADHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or devoted backer of a cause, party or person.

clue.text: Hairstyle for each male

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: A barber's price list showing a set hairstyle charge for every man.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for permanent wave, a chemically set curly hairdo.

clue.text: Earnest request reversing Nebraska pact

indicators.note: reversing tells you to write the state's abbreviation the other way round

parts.note: NE is the US postal abbreviation for Nebraska
a pact is a treaty

explanation.surface: A plea that the state of Nebraska go back on an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea or earnest appeal; a heartfelt asking.

clue.text: Retiring party nearly having no space left

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something with no room left is full

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a party just before it got too crowded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests leaving or stopping work but means shy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring here is an adjective meaning shy and self-effacing, a synonym.

clue.text: Is the person speaking to leave, chum?

parts.note: said by the speaker, is becomes am, with I as the person: am I
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A speaker asking a pal whether they ought to depart.
explanation.walkthrough: Asking 'Is the person speaking …?' from the speaker's own mouth gives 'Am I …?'
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for friend, used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: Tell Elvis, on the move, to load piano on various planes

indicators.note: to load means to put something inside, so the piano letter goes within the jumble
letters on the move are shifted into a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Removal men told to get Elvis's piano into the truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' gives SLITLEVEL from TELL ELVIS; 'to load' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a building or room with floors at different heights.

clue.text: New name in oil, say, to pour through a narrow opening

indicators.note: in places the two single letters inside the word for oil

parts.note: oil is an example of fuel

explanation.surface: Decanting a fresh brand of oil through a narrow neck.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to channel a liquid through a cone-shaped tube.

clue.text: Serious actor, one in Dickensian musical

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the musical's title

parts.note: Oliver! is the stage musical based on Dickens's Oliver Twist
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A heavyweight thespian taking a part in a Dickens-based show.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence, the celebrated British stage and screen actor known for Shakespeare roles.

clue.text: Giant songbird, along with missing tail

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: missing tail says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: along with means and

explanation.surface: A huge songbird that has lost its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a race of enormous deities; any huge or mighty person.

clue.text: With prophetic sign, curse female habits

parts.note: an omen is a sign of what is to come
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Bad language from someone foreseeing doom over feminine behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' suggests customs, but it means clothing, as in a nun's or riding habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Habits in the sense of garments, so clothing for ladies.

clue.text: Office equipment, not so modern, securing page

indicators.note: securing means holding something inside, so the page letter is enclosed

parts.note: staler means older, less fresh

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned office kit that fastens sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk device that fastens sheets of paper with wire clips.

clue.text: Environmentalist ignoring leader, to attempt getting in again

indicators.note: ignoring leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party
to attempt is to try

explanation.surface: An eco-activist defying their chief to try returning to the movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of coming back in, as a spacecraft into the atmosphere.

clue.text: Nurse in operation for sinew

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
a machine in operation is on

explanation.surface: A nurse in theatre dealing with a damaged sinew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' suggests surgery but means simply working, giving ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone, a synonym.

clue.text: Organised arrangement made unhappy when parts are switched

indicators.note: the two halves of the word swap places

parts.note: upset means made unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone distressed when a neat system has its parts muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: UPSET's two halves, UP and SET, change places.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation or system of how things are arranged.

clue.text: Greek character following Greek woman (who wanted privacy?)

indicators.note: following says the Greek letter comes after the abbreviation

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek woman seeking to be left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket alludes to Garbo, the film star famed for 'I want to be alone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, famously that of reclusive screen star Garbo.
